name: Dubai, UAE
clues: I'm so tall that Tom Cruise had to climb my outside with sticky gloves. I'm the tallest building in the world. Where am I?
The Burj Khalifa, in this glitzy desert city in the United Arab Emirates.
The biggest city in the UAE, on the Persian Gulf.
fact: Tom Cruise did the climb himself, attached to safety cables.

name: San Francisco, USA
clues: Riley's emotions panicked when her family moved to my hilly city, where even the pizza had broccoli on it. Look for a red bridge in the fog. Where am I?
Riley moves here from Minnesota. My Golden Gate Bridge is famous everywhere.
A city on the coast of Northern California.
fact: Inside Out 2 (2024) became one of the highest-grossing animated movies ever.

name: Atlanta, USA
clues: Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn. Scarlett O'Hara fled as my city burned in the Civil War. Where am I?
Gone with the Wind's big fire scene is the burning of this Georgia city.
The capital of Georgia, in the southeast USA.
fact: Margaret Mitchell wrote Gone with the Wind in her Atlanta apartment.

from: 🎬 Star Wars: Attack of the Clones
name: Lake Como, Italy
clues: Anakin and Padmé had their secret wedding at a villa on my shore. I'm a lake shaped like an upside-down Y. Where am I?
Lake Como, in northern Italy near the Swiss border.
Northern Italy, north of Milan.
fact: The wedding was filmed at Villa del Balbianello, which also appears in Casino Royale.

name: Forks, Washington, USA
clues: It rains so much in my small town that vampires can go out in the daytime. Team Edward or Team Jacob? Where am I?
Twilight is set in Forks, a small town in Washington State.
The Olympic Peninsula, in the far northwest corner of Washington State.
fact: Forks is one of the rainiest towns in the USA.

name: Singapore
clues: Rachel thought she was meeting her boyfriend's family. Turns out they're crazy rich, with parties at a rooftop pool shaped like a ship. Where am I?
Crazy Rich Asians is set in this tiny, rich island country with the Marina Bay Sands hotel.
A city-state at the southern tip of Malaysia.
fact: Crazy Rich Asians is based on Kevin Kwan's 2013 novel.

name: Moscow, Russia
clues: Napoleon marched all the way to me and found me empty and on fire. My red fortress is called the Kremlin. Where am I?
Tolstoy's War and Peace shows Napoleon taking this Russian city in 1812.
The capital of Russia.
fact: War and Peace is more than 1,000 pages long.

name: Swiss Alps
clues: An orphan girl was sent to live with her grumpy grandfather on my mountain and fell in love with the goats and meadows. Where am I?
Heidi is set in the Alps of this country, famous for chocolate and watches.
Eastern Switzerland, near Liechtenstein.
fact: Heidi was written in 1881 and is one of the best-selling books ever.

name: La Mancha, Spain
clues: An old knight charged at my windmills because he thought they were giants. Where am I?
Don Quixote comes from La Mancha, a flat region of central Spain full of windmills.
Central Spain, south of Madrid.
fact: Don Quixote, from 1605, is often called the first modern novel.

name: Pangong Lake, India
clues: At the end of 3 Idiots, the friends finally find Rancho by my lake. I'm 4,000 meters up and change color through the day. Where am I?
Pangong Lake, high in the mountains of Ladakh, India.
Far northern India, on the border with Tibet.
fact: 3 Idiots (2009) was one of the biggest Indian movies of its time.

name: Pyramids of Giza, Egypt
clues: A shepherd boy dreamed of treasure buried at my feet, so he crossed the whole desert to find it. I'm 4,500 years old and shaped like triangles. Where am I?
In The Alchemist, Santiago travels from Spain to these famous pyramids in Egypt.
Right next to Cairo, the capital of Egypt.
fact: The Alchemist by Paulo Coelho is one of the best-selling books of all time.

name: Mount Rushmore, USA
clues: Four presidents' faces are carved into me, and Cary Grant dangled from their noses in North by Northwest. Where am I?
Mount Rushmore, in the Black Hills.
South Dakota, in the northern Great Plains of the USA.
fact: Each face on Mount Rushmore is about 18 meters (60 feet) tall.

name: Yosemite, USA
clues: A man climbed my 900-meter granite wall with no rope at all. The movie about it, Free Solo, won an Oscar. Where am I?
El Capitan, in Yosemite National Park.
California's Sierra Nevada mountains.
fact: Alex Honnold climbed El Capitan without ropes in 2017, in under four hours.

name: Mont-Saint-Michel, France
clues: Rapunzel's kingdom is an island town that climbs a rock up to a castle, and it was inspired by me. At high tide, the sea surrounds me. Where am I?
Mont-Saint-Michel, an island abbey off the coast of Normandy.
Northwest France, between Normandy and Brittany.
fact: The tides around Mont-Saint-Michel are some of the biggest in Europe.

name: Helsingør, Denmark
clues: To be or not to be. A prince sees his father's ghost on the walls of my castle. Where am I?
Hamlet's Elsinore is Kronborg Castle in Helsingør, Denmark.
Northeast Denmark, across the water from Sweden.
fact: Hamlet is performed at Kronborg Castle almost every summer.

name: Scottish Highlands
clues: Merida shot for her own hand and turned her mum into a bear. Her kingdom of misty highlands, castles and lochs is on a real map. Where am I?
Brave takes place in this country at the north end of Great Britain.
The northern part of the United Kingdom.
fact: Merida is voiced by Scottish actress Kelly Macdonald.

name: Grand Canyon, USA
clues: Two friends on the run hit the gas and flew off my edge instead of giving up. I'm a mile deep and carved by a river. Where am I?
Thelma & Louise ends at this giant canyon carved by the Colorado River.
Northern Arizona, USA.
fact: The final scene was actually filmed at Dead Horse Point in Utah.

name: Aswan, Egypt
clues: Hercule Poirot goes on a river cruise past ancient temples, and of course, someone gets murdered on the boat. Where am I?
Death on the Nile begins at a famous hotel in this city in southern Egypt.
Southern Egypt, on the Nile, near the big dam.
fact: Agatha Christie stayed at the Old Cataract Hotel in Aswan.

name: Salzburg, Austria
clues: The hills are alive with the sound of music! Maria sang and danced with seven kids through my gardens and mountains. Where am I?
The Sound of Music takes place in this Austrian city, where Mozart was born.
Austria, right by the German border.
fact: Mozart was born in Salzburg in 1756.

name: Nantucket, USA
clues: Call me Ishmael. Captain Ahab's whaling ship sailed from my little island to hunt a white whale. Where am I?
Moby-Dick's ship sails from Nantucket, an island off Massachusetts.
An island south of Cape Cod, Massachusetts.
fact: Nantucket was the whaling capital of the world in the early 1800s.

name: Chicago, USA
clues: My family flew to Paris and forgot me at home for Christmas, so I fought off two burglars with paint cans and a tarantula in a big house outside my city. Where am I?
Kevin McCallister's house is in a suburb of this windy city on Lake Michigan.
The biggest city in Illinois, on Lake Michigan.
fact: The real Home Alone house is in Winnetka, just north of Chicago.

name: Milan, Italy
clues: My country is shaped like a boot, and here people wear their best ones. Miranda Priestly flew in to sit in the front row at my fashion week. Where am I?
Italy's fashion capital, in the north, not far from the Alps.
The big city in northern Italy, between Turin and Venice.
fact: The sequel filmed at a real Dolce & Gabbana show during Milan Fashion Week in 2025.

from: 🎬 Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
name: Petra, Jordan
clues: Indiana Jones rode up to my pink stone front door looking for the Holy Grail. I'm a whole city carved into a cliff. Where am I?
The Last Crusade's ending was filmed at the Treasury in Petra, an ancient city.
Southern Jordan, in the Middle East.
fact: Petra was carved by the Nabataeans more than 2,000 years ago.

name: Area 51, Nevada, USA
clues: I don't officially exist, but in Independence Day the President found a crashed alien spaceship hidden under my desert. Where am I?
Area 51, the secret air base in the Nevada desert.
Southern Nevada, north of Las Vegas.
fact: The US government only officially admitted Area 51 exists in 2013.

name: Haworth, England
clues: Heathcliff and Cathy ran wild across my windy moors. Emily Brontë wrote the book while living in my village. Where am I?
Wuthering Heights is set on the Yorkshire moors around Haworth, England.
Northern England, west of Leeds.
fact: A new Wuthering Heights movie with Margot Robbie came out in 2026.

name: Toronto, Canada
clues: Whenever Mei gets too excited, she poofs into a giant red panda, right in the middle of my city, under my tall CN Tower. Where am I?
Turning Red is set in this big Canadian city on Lake Ontario.
Canada's biggest city, on Lake Ontario.
fact: Turning Red is set in 2002, and Mei's family looks after a temple in Toronto's Chinatown.

name: Berlin, Germany
clues: A wall cut my city in half for 28 years. In Bridge of Spies, two spies are swapped on a bridge at my edge during the Cold War. Where am I?
The Berlin Wall split this German capital from 1961 to 1989.
The capital of Germany.
fact: The real spy swap of 1962 happened on the Glienicke Bridge between Berlin and Potsdam.

name: Fargo, North Dakota, USA
clues: The movie is named after me, but almost none of it happens here. Most of it is across the river in snowy Minnesota. Where am I?
Fargo is a city in North Dakota.
Eastern North Dakota, on the Minnesota border.
fact: Fargo (1996) won Oscars for Frances McDormand and for its screenplay.

from: 📖 A Song of Ice and Fire
name: Dubrovnik, Croatia
clues: Winter is coming, but not to me. My old city walls played King's Landing in Game of Thrones. Where am I?
This walled city on Croatia's coast played King's Landing on screen.
Southern Croatia, on the Adriatic Sea.
fact: Dubrovnik's city walls are almost 2 km long.

name: Canyonlands, Utah, USA
clues: A hiker got his arm stuck under a boulder in my slot canyon for 127 hours, and got out the hardest way possible. Where am I?
127 Hours happened in Blue John Canyon, in the Utah desert.
Southeast Utah, next to Canyonlands National Park.
fact: Aron Ralston, the real hiker, kept climbing mountains afterward.

name: Dunkirk, France
clues: Soldiers were trapped on my beach, so ordinary people sailed their little boats across the sea to bring them home. The movie has my name. Where am I?
Christopher Nolan's Dunkirk: a French port on the English Channel, in 1940.
A port in northern France, near Belgium.
fact: More than 330,000 soldiers were rescued from Dunkirk in 1940.

name: Sydney, Australia
clues: P. Sherman, 42 Wallaby Way. A dad fish swam across the ocean to find that address and his son, in my harbor. Where am I?
Nemo ends up in a dentist's fish tank in this Australian city, famous for its Opera House.
The biggest city in Australia, on the southeast coast.
fact: Marlin swims from the Great Barrier Reef all the way down the coast to Sydney Harbour.

name: Buenos Aires, Argentina
clues: Don't cry for me! Eva Perón sang to the crowds from the balcony of the Pink House in my city. Where am I?
Evita is about Argentina's first lady. The Casa Rosada is in this capital.
The capital of Argentina.
fact: Madonna sang from the real Casa Rosada balcony for Evita.

name: Colombia
clues: We don't talk about Bruno, but we do talk about me: the magic family's house, mountains and coffee fields come from my country. Where am I?
Encanto takes place in this South American country, famous for coffee.
The top of South America, next to Panama.
fact: 'We Don't Talk About Bruno' hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

name: Zhangjiajie, China
clues: My stone pillars poke out of the clouds like floating mountains. Avatar's Hallelujah Mountains were inspired by me. Where am I?
Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, in China.
Hunan province, in south-central China.
fact: One of Zhangjiajie's pillars was renamed 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain' after the movie.

name: New York City, USA
clues: Santa's sleigh crash-landed in my park, and an elf in yellow tights went looking for his dad. The best way to spread Christmas cheer is singing loud for all to hear. Where am I?
Buddy the Elf travels from the North Pole to this city. Santa lands in Central Park.
The biggest city in the USA.
fact: Elf (2003) was directed by Jon Favreau, who also plays the doctor.

name: Las Vegas, USA
clues: What happens here stays here. Four friends woke up with a tiger in the bathroom and no memory of last night in my city. Where am I?
The Hangover's bachelor party goes wrong in this desert city of casinos.
A casino city in the Nevada desert.
fact: Caesars Palace, where the guys stay in The Hangover, opened in 1966.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle, Germany
clues: I'm the real castle that inspired Sleeping Beauty's, the one Disney fans know by heart. A 'fairy-tale king' built me on a hill. Where am I?
Neuschwanstein Castle, in Bavaria.
Southern Germany, near the Austrian border.
fact: King Ludwig II started building Neuschwanstein in 1869.

name: Memphis, USA
clues: The King of Rock and Roll lived in a mansion called Graceland in my city. Thank you, thank you very much. Where am I?
Elvis recorded his first songs at Sun Studio in this Tennessee city on the Mississippi.
Tennessee's biggest city, in the southwest corner.
fact: Graceland is one of the most visited homes in the USA.

name: Pench, India
clues: A boy raised by wolves made friends with a bear and a panther in my jungle. Kipling set The Jungle Book in my hills. Where am I?
The Jungle Book takes place around Seoni, in central India, where Pench National Park is now.
Madhya Pradesh, right in the middle of India.
fact: Pench National Park is home to real Bengal tigers like Shere Khan.

name: Boston, USA
clues: A janitor at a famous university solved the math problems nobody else could. How do you like them apples? Where am I?
Good Will Hunting is set in this city and next door at MIT and Harvard.
The biggest city in New England, on the coast of Massachusetts.
fact: Matt Damon and Ben Affleck won the Oscar for writing Good Will Hunting.

name: Alaska, USA
clues: A young man gave away his savings and walked into my wilderness to live off the land, inside an old abandoned bus. Where am I?
Into the Wild ends in the biggest US state, far to the north.
The far northwest corner of North America, next to Canada. The bus was near Denali.
fact: The real bus was airlifted out in 2020 and is now at a museum in Fairbanks.

name: Belfast, Northern Ireland
clues: The ship that 'couldn't sink' was built in my shipyard. Jack and Rose met on board, and it didn't end well. Where am I?
The Titanic was built in this city in Northern Ireland.
The capital of Northern Ireland.
fact: Titanic Belfast, a museum shaped like ship bows, stands where the ship was built.

name: Maya Bay, Thailand
clues: A backpacker found a map to a secret paradise beach. It turned out to be me, a lagoon walled in by cliffs, and now everyone knows. Where am I?
The Beach was filmed at Maya Bay, in Thailand's Phi Phi Islands.
Southern Thailand, near Phuket.
fact: Maya Bay was closed for years to let its coral recover from too many tourists.

name: Galápagos Islands, Ecuador
clues: Darwin studied my giant tortoises and finches and came up with evolution. In Master and Commander, the ship's doctor explores my islands. Where am I?
The Galápagos Islands, in the Pacific Ocean.
In the Pacific, about 1,000 km west of Ecuador.
fact: Galápagos giant tortoises can live for more than 100 years.

name: London, England
clues: Love actually is all around, especially at Christmas. A boy runs through my airport and a prime minister dances down the stairs in my city. Where am I?
Love Actually starts and ends at Heathrow, this city's big airport.
The capital of the United Kingdom.
fact: Love Actually opens and closes with real footage of people hugging at Heathrow arrivals.

name: Kansas, USA
clues: There's no place like home, and Dorothy's home is me. Just keep an eye on the sky: my tornadoes can blow you all the way to Oz. Where am I?
A flat, farm-filled state right in the middle of the USA.
In the center of the USA, between Colorado and Missouri.
fact: L. Frank Baum's book came out in 1900, and the famous movie followed in 1939.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro, Tanzania
clues: I'm a mountain with snow on top, even though I'm close to the equator. Hemingway wrote about my snows. Where am I?
Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's tallest mountain.
Northern Tanzania, near the Kenyan border.
fact: Kilimanjaro is 5,895 meters tall.

name: Detroit, USA
clues: You only get one shot. Eminem's character battle-rapped his way up from a trailer park on the road that marks my city's edge. Where am I?
8 Mile is a real road on the north edge of this Michigan city, the Motor City.
Michigan's biggest city, across the river from Canada.
fact: Eminem won an Oscar for 'Lose Yourself' from 8 Mile.

name: Aït Benhaddou, Morocco
clues: Before he fought in Rome, Maximus battled as a slave in a mud-brick town in my North African country. Where am I?
Gladiator filmed its slave-arena scenes at Aït Benhaddou, a walled village in Morocco.
Central Morocco, near Ouarzazate, south of the Atlas Mountains.
fact: Aït Benhaddou has also appeared in Game of Thrones.

name: New York City, USA
clues: A kid bit by a spider swings over my street, / past yellow cabs honking and pretzels to eat. / They call me a fruit, but I'm concrete and light, / and I never once close my eyes for the night.
Peter's from Queens, just a short subway ride / from Times Square and Broadway on the other side.
America's biggest, on the Atlantic shore, / where a lady in green holds a torch by the door.
fact: Peter Parker has been a Queens kid since his very first comic in 1962.

name: Cleveland, USA
clues: A man made of steel was dreamed up on my lake / by two teenage boys with some comics to make. / I played his big city when the cameras came round, / and I'm also the hall where rock music is crowned.
Jerry and Joe drew him back in '33, / in a Great Lakes city with a Rock Hall to see.
Look in Ohio, where Lake Erie's waves roll: / the north-coast city of rock and roll.
fact: Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster created Superman in Cleveland in the 1930s.

name: Abu Dhabi, UAE
clues: The race starts at sunset and ends in the night, / under a hotel made of thousands of lights. / Brad Pitt takes his last lap on my desert-side bay, / in a capital city that's sunny all day.
The season's last Grand Prix finishes here, / at Yas Marina's track at the end of the year.
The capital city of the UAE, / a short drive from Dubai, by the Gulf's warm sea.
fact: F1 filmed during the real 2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix weekend.

name: Troy, Turkey
clues: They left me a gift on the beach, made of wood, / and my people all cheered, for it looked very good. / By night it unloaded a hidden surprise, / and Odysseus sailed from my ashes and cries.
My ruins sit in Turkey, not Greece, which is odd / for a war fought by heroes and blessed by a god.
Look in northwest Turkey, by the Dardanelles strait, / near Çanakkale, where my old walls still wait.
fact: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey (2026) is based on Homer's ancient poem.

name: Mount Everest, Nepal
clues: I'm the roof of the world, with my head in the sky, / where the air is so thin even eagles don't fly. / Climbers queue up for days just to stand on my crown, / then they hurry like crazy to get themselves down.
On the border of Nepal and Tibet I stand tall, / the highest of the Himalayas, the highest of all.
The tallest mountain on Earth, you know my name: / nearly nine kilometers of frozen-rock fame.
fact: Everest is 8,849 meters tall, according to a 2020 measurement.

name: Goa, India
clues: A spy with no memory hid on my sand, / with hammocks and palm trees and cashews at hand. / But a killer still found him, so off he would race / from the tiniest state of a huge, crowded place.
Portuguese churches and beach parties too, / on India's west coast, by an ocean of blue.
India's smallest state, on the Arabian Sea, / south of Mumbai. Now where could I be?
fact: Goa was a Portuguese colony until 1961.

name: Oklahoma, USA
clues: When my sky turns to green and the sirens all wail, / most people take cover from wind and from hail. / But storm chasers floor it and drive toward the spin, / through my wide-open plains, where the twisters begin.
I'm in Tornado Alley, the heart of the US, / shaped like a pan with a handle, I guess.
Just north of Texas, my panhandle sticks west; / sign me in short and I'm 'OK' at best.
fact: Oklahoma gets dozens of tornadoes in a typical year.

name: Concord, Massachusetts, USA
clues: Four sisters, one writer, a house full of plays, / with Jo scribbling stories for most of her days. / The real author lived here through New England's fall, / where the 'shot heard round the world' started it all.
Near Walden Pond, where Thoreau lived alone, / a short drive from Boston, I'm Louisa's old home.
In Massachusetts, by Lexington's side, / northwest of Boston, a half-hour ride.
fact: Orchard House, where Alcott wrote Little Women, is now a museum.

name: Sicily, Italy
clues: I'm the ball that gets kicked by a boot in the sea, / and a crime family borrowed its last name from me. / Michael hid in my hills when New York got too hot, / where a volcano still smokes on the top of the lot.
Mount Etna still smokes on my eastern side, / just off Italy's toe, a short ferry ride.
The biggest island in the Mediterranean Sea, / at the tip of Italy's boot. That's me.
fact: Corleone is a real town in Sicily, south of Palermo.

name: Omaha Beach, Normandy, France
clues: On a grey June morning, the boats hit my sand, / and thousands of soldiers came charging to land. / Then a squad went to find just one private and bring / him home from my beach, where the cold waters sting.
My code name was Omaha, though I'm far from Nebraska, / on the coast of France (a long way from Alaska).
In Normandy, France, on the English Channel shore, / where D-Day began in the Second World War.
fact: D-Day took place on June 6, 1944.

name: Monument Valley, USA
clues: A man ran for years, coast to coast, then he stopped / on my long empty road where the red towers popped. / He said he was tired and he'd go home instead, / and my rocks stood behind him, all dusty and red.
I'm on Navajo land where the cowboy films played, / with sandstone buttes towering, casting their shade.
On the Utah-Arizona line, my red buttes stand, / in the Navajo Nation's wide desert land.
fact: The spot on US Route 163 is now nicknamed Forrest Gump Point.

name: Pondicherry, India
clues: A boy and a tiger, one boat, lots of sea, / two hundred-odd days, but the trip began with me. / His family's zoo was in my seaside town, / where the streets have French names and the cafés slow down.
France ruled me once, on India's southeast shore, / by the Bay of Bengal, where the warm breezes pour.
South of Chennai, on India's east coast I lie; / my new name is Puducherry. Give it a try.
fact: Life of Pi won four Oscars, including Best Director for Ang Lee.

name: Mumbai, India
clues: A kid from my slums was one question from riches, / but they thought he was cheating and searched him for glitches. / I'm the home of the movies with dancing and song, / a huge city by the sea where the trains are packed long.
Bollywood's mine, and the Gateway of India too, / on India's west coast, by the Arabian blue.
India's biggest city, once known as Bombay, / on the west coast. Now pin me, OK?
fact: Slumdog Millionaire won eight Oscars, including Best Picture.

name: Dublin, Ireland
clues: A book like a brick takes place all in one day, / as a man walks my streets and he wanders his way. / Each June the fans dress up in hats from back then, / and they read the whole thing in my pubs once again.
My river's the Liffey, my beer's dark as night, / I'm an island's capital, where the grass is so bright.
The capital of Ireland, by the Irish Sea, / home of the Guinness Storehouse. That's me.
fact: June 16 is celebrated in Dublin as Bloomsday.

name: Kraków, Poland
clues: A businessman saved them, one list at a time, / more than a thousand, while war spread its crime. / His factory stood in my old royal town, / where a castle on a hill still looks proudly down.
In southern Poland, my market square's grand, / one of the biggest old town squares in the land.
Poland's old royal capital, by the Vistula's flow, / south of Warsaw. Now where do you go?
fact: Oskar Schindler's factory in Kraków is now a museum.

name: Monroeville, Alabama, USA
clues: A girl they called Scout and her lawyer dad / lived in a sleepy town, both good and bad. / The writer grew up on my courthouse-square streets, / where the summers were slow under sweltering heat.
Harper Lee grew up here; my old courthouse still stands, / a small southern town out in cotton-field lands.
In southwest Alabama, a small county seat, / the real-life Maycomb, where the mockingbirds tweet.
fact: Harper Lee's childhood friend Truman Capote inspired the character Dill.

name: Tokyo, Japan
clues: A giant gray lizard comes up from my bay; / he stomps on my buildings, then wanders away. / I'm the biggest of cities, I always rebuild, / with neon and trains and my sushi bars filled.
My Shibuya crossing's the busiest around, / in an island country where bullet trains sound.
The capital of Japan, on the island of Honshu, / with Mount Fuji nearby. Now you know what to do.
fact: Godzilla Minus One won the Oscar for Best Visual Effects in 2024.

name: Pamplona, Spain
clues: Each July, people run with some very big friends / down my narrow old streets till the bull run ends. / Hemingway drank here and wrote it all down, / so the whole world now comes to my party in town.
San Fermín is my festival, red scarves and white, / near the Pyrenees mountains, partying all night.
In northern Spain, Navarre's capital, see? / The running of the bulls happens here, at me.
fact: The festival is called San Fermín and runs July 6 to 14.

name: Naples, Italy
clues: Two girls, best friends and rivals, grow up on my streets, / with a smoking volcano that looms over their seats. / I'm noisy and messy and loud as can be, / and I gave the world pizza. You're welcome, from me.
Mount Vesuvius watches over my bay; / Pompeii's not far, just a short train away.
Southern Italy's biggest city by the sea, / home of the margherita. That's me.
fact: Pizza Margherita is said to have been named in Naples for Queen Margherita in 1889.

name: New Orleans, USA
clues: A girl kissed a frog and she turned into one, / and they hopped through my bayous, all jazz and all fun. / My streets fill with parades and with beads in the air, / and gumbo and beignets are cooking out there.
Mardi Gras is my party, the French Quarter my heart, / where the Mississippi and the Gulf aren't far apart.
Louisiana's biggest city, where jazz was born, they say, / on the Mississippi, near the Gulf of Mexico's bay.
fact: Tiana was Disney's first African American princess.

name: Verona, Italy
clues: Two families fighting, two kids in a rush, / a balcony, poison, and one final hush. / Today people write love notes to her in my town, / and a Roman arena still stands, safe and sound.
Near Lake Garda in Italy's north I lie, / where a famous balcony draws every passerby.
In Italy's Veneto, west of Venice, you'll see / the city of Romeo and Juliet: me.
fact: Volunteers called the Juliet Club answer thousands of letters to Juliet every year.

name: Nottingham, England
clues: An archer in green stole the gold of the rich, / then he gave it away to the poor without a hitch. / He hid in my forest from a sheriff's mean crew, / under oak trees so old they've seen centuries through.
Sherwood Forest is my backyard green, / in the English Midlands, where outlaws were seen.
A city in the English Midlands, whose sheriff, they say, / chased Robin Hood around day after day.
fact: The Major Oak in Sherwood Forest is said to have been Robin Hood's hideout.

name: Dawson City, Canada
clues: A dog stolen south was dragged north through the snow / to pull sleds for the miners where gold rivers flow. / Thousands came rushing to dig for my gold, / in a land where the winters are terribly cold.
The Klondike Gold Rush made me boom overnight, / in Canada's far north, near Alaska's border site.
In Yukon, Canada, where two rivers meet, / a gold-rush town with old wooden streets.
fact: Jack London went to the Klondike himself in 1897.

name: Seoul, South Korea
clues: A poor family sneaks in, one job at a time, / to a rich family's house up a long hill to climb. / The rich live up high and the poor live below, / in my city of K-pop and neon aglow.
Gangnam's my style and kimchi's my snack; / the Han River runs through me, front to back.
South Korea's capital, a big city of tens of millions, / where K-dramas get filmed, and the views are brilliant.
fact: Parasite won Best Picture in 2020, the first film not in English to do it.

name: Marseille, France
clues: Locked in an island jail for a crime he didn't do, / he dug and he waited for fourteen years through. / He escaped in a sack, got rich, then came back / to my sunny old port where the fishing boats pack.
The Château d'If is the prison out in my bay; / I'm France's oldest city, by the Med, they say.
France's big port on the Mediterranean shore, / its second-largest city, with fish soup galore.
fact: The Château d'If is a real fortress, and you can visit it by boat.

name: Salem, Massachusetts, USA
clues: Three witchy sisters came back from the dead / when a boy lit a candle that burned black instead. / My town held real witch trials centuries ago; / now each Halloween I put on quite a show.
In 1692 my witch trials went wrong; / now costumes and ghost tours fill October long.
A Massachusetts town north of Boston by the sea, / they call me the Witch City. That's me.
fact: Salem throws a giant Halloween festival every October.

name: Matera, Italy
clues: A spy's silver car spun in circles in my square, / while bullets bounced off it and smoke filled the air. / My houses are caves carved in rock long ago, / in the arch of the boot, way down south and below.
My Sassi cave homes are some of the oldest around, / in southern Italy, where stone streets abound.
In Basilicata, southern Italy's arch, / the City of Stones, where James Bond made his march.
fact: Matera's cave homes, the Sassi, are among the oldest lived-in places in the world.

name: Kauai, Hawaii, USA
clues: A small blue alien crashed onto my sand, / and a girl taught him 'ohana' on my island land. / I'm the oldest and greenest of my island chain, / with emerald cliffs that are drenched by the rain.
They call me the Garden Isle, the chain's northern end, / in the 50th state, where the surfers ascend.
In Hawaii, northwest of Oahu across the sea, / the Garden Isle. Now where could I be?
fact: The original 2002 movie is set on Kauai, and its little town was inspired by Hanapepe.

name: Edinburgh, Scotland
clues: Renton went racing down my streets on the run, / in a film that showed my dark side, not just fun. / A castle sits high on a rock that once burned, / and each August my streets into theaters are turned.
My Fringe is the world's biggest arts festival show; / I'm a capital up north, where the bagpipes blow.
Scotland's capital city, with a castle on high, / and Arthur's Seat hill reaching up to the sky.
fact: J.K. Rowling wrote early Harry Potter chapters in Edinburgh cafés.

name: St. Petersburg, Russia
clues: A lost princess danced in my palace one night, / before revolution put out all my light. / A tsar built me up from a cold, soggy swamp, / with canals and white nights and imperial pomp.
The Hermitage fills my Winter Palace halls, / in a land where in June the night hardly falls.
Russia's second city, on the Baltic Sea, / once its capital, founded by Peter. That's me.
fact: The Winter Palace in St. Petersburg is now the Hermitage Museum.

name: Ha Long Bay, Vietnam
clues: A giant ape rules on an island of mist; / my green water's dotted with stone, twist after twist. / Old junk boats glide through me with sails orange-red, / and thousands of islands rise up from my bed.
Kong: Skull Island filmed in my limestone maze, / in Southeast Asia, by the Gulf of Tonkin's haze.
In northern Vietnam, east of Hanoi by the sea, / a famous bay of rock islands. That's me.
fact: Ha Long Bay has more than 1,600 islands.

name: Paris, France
clues: A code hides behind the world's most famous smile, / in a museum topped with glass in a pyramid style. / An iron tower sparkles each hour at night, / and croissants come warm from my bakeries' light.
The Louvre is mine, and so is the Seine, / where artists and lovers walk again and again.
The capital of France, the City of Light, / with its tall iron tower glowing at night.
fact: The Louvre's glass pyramid was finished in 1989 and is now the museum's main entrance.

name: Johannesburg, South Africa
clues: A president used just one rugby team / to bring a whole country together in a dream. / They won the World Cup final in my stadium's roar, / in a city built on gold from the rock to the core.
My Soweto township was Mandela's old home; / I'm the biggest city where the springboks roam.
South Africa's biggest city, high up inland, / they call me Jozi, built on gold-rush sand.
fact: Morgan Freeman played Mandela in Invictus.

name: Kyoto, Japan
clues: A girl sold as a child grew up in my lanes, / in silk and white makeup, through lessons and pains. / I was Japan's capital a thousand years long, / with a temple of gold and a bamboo grove's song.
Gion's my geisha district, with teahouses old, / and thousands of orange shrine gates, I'm told.
Japan's old imperial capital, near Osaka's side, / home of the Golden Pavilion, with temples worldwide.
fact: Kyoto was Japan's capital for more than 1,000 years.

name: Fiji
clues: A delivery man washed up alone on my shore / with a volleyball buddy and nothing much more. / He learned to make fire, then he sailed off at last / from my South Pacific islands, palm-fringed and vast.
My three hundred islands say 'Bula!' to you, / north of New Zealand, in the South Pacific blue.
A South Pacific island nation, Suva's my capital town, / where a castaway spent four years with the sun beating down.
fact: Monuriki is part of Fiji's Mamanuca Islands.

name: Rome, Italy
clues: Two thousand years back, fighters battled in my ring, / with lions and crowds and a thumbs-down from the king. / My ruins are everywhere, my coins fill a fountain, / and I was built on seven hills, not one mountain.
The Colosseum's mine, and the Vatican's in me too, / Italy's capital, with the Tiber flowing through.
Italy's capital, the Eternal City by name, / where all roads lead, so they say. Same old fame.
fact: Historians think the real Colosseum may have been flooded for mock sea battles in its early years.

name: Liverpool, England
clues: A singer woke up in a world with no Fab Four, / so he sang all their songs and the crowds wanted more. / The real band began in a cellar of mine, / in a port by the sea where the ferries all shine.
The Cavern Club's here, and two football teams too, / on the River Mersey, with an Irish Sea view.
A port city in northwest England, on the Mersey's shore, / home of the Beatles and their songs galore.
fact: Penny Lane and Strawberry Field, from Beatles songs, are real places in Liverpool.

name: Los Alamos, USA
clues: On a mesa, in secret, a town sprang up fast, / where scientists built something that went off with a blast. / You couldn't find me on any map back then, / in a high desert state of red rock and green chile again.
The Manhattan Project's lab was hidden right here, / in the mountains of New Mexico, with Santa Fe near.
In northern New Mexico, northwest of Santa Fe, / a lab town on mesas, still working today.
fact: Oppenheimer won seven Oscars in 2024, including Best Picture.

name: Gary, Indiana, USA
clues: I sound like a guy's name, not a place on the map, / and five singing brothers grew up in my lap. / The youngest became the biggest pop king, / from a tiny brick house where they practiced to sing.
I'm a steel-mill city on Lake Michigan's shore, / near Chicago, in a state where race cars roar.
In northwest Indiana, just southeast of Chicago, see, / the Jackson 5's hometown. That's me.
fact: The Jackson family's house at 2300 Jackson Street had just two bedrooms.

name: Belfast, Northern Ireland
clues: I built a great liner, the biggest afloat; / they swore that no iceberg could sink such a boat. / Jack and Rose sailed on her, and you know how that went, / but my shipyard's still proud of the steel that it bent.
Two big yellow cranes tower over my docks, / in the UK's piece of an island of green hills and rocks.
Northern Ireland's capital, on its east coast by the sea, / with a Titanic museum. Now where could I be?
fact: Titanic was built at Belfast's Harland & Wolff shipyard, and the Titanic Belfast museum stands right beside the slipway where she was launched in 1911.

name: Salzburg, Austria
clues: A nun turned a nanny for seven, and then / she taught them to sing in my gardens again. / A famous composer was born on my street, / and a castle on top makes my skyline complete.
I'm near the Alps, on the German border line, / in a country of mountains, of strudel and wine.
In Austria, where the Salzach River flows, / Mozart's hometown, where the do-re-mi tour goes.
fact: The Sound of Music was filmed in and around Salzburg in 1964. Mozart was born there in 1756.

name: Hobbiton, Matamata, New Zealand
clues: Round doors in green hillsides, a party tree too, / where small folk with big feet eat breakfast times two. / The wizards and rings were all filmed on my farm, / in a country of sheep with a whole lot of charm.
Bilbo's round door still sits in my hill, / on a sheep farm the tourists come visiting still.
Near Matamata, on New Zealand's North Isle, / the Hobbiton set will make any fan smile.
fact: Hobbiton was built on a working sheep farm near Matamata. After The Hobbit films it was rebuilt to last, and now more than half a million people visit a year.

name: Burj Khalifa, Dubai, UAE
clues: A spy climbed my glass with just gloves that could stick, / a hundred-plus floors up, and he had to be quick. / I'm the tallest of all, I poke right through the cloud, / in a desert-side city that loves to be loud.
Tom Cruise really climbed me, outside, on a rope, / in a Gulf city of malls and of skyscraper hope.
The world's tallest building, in Dubai by the sea; / the Burj Khalifa. Now point there to me.
fact: Tom Cruise did the Burj Khalifa climb himself, hanging from cables more than 120 floors up.

from: 🎬 Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
name: Petra, Jordan
clues: A man in a fedora rode up to my gate / for a cup from the Last Supper, holy and great. / I wasn't built: I was carved from the rock, / pink cliffs and a canyon you walk through in shock.
Through a narrow canyon called the Siq you creep, / to a treasury carved where the desert sands sleep.
In southern Jordan, the Rose City of stone, / an ancient desert town, carved and alone.
fact: The temple Indiana Jones rides up to is Petra's Treasury, carved into a sandstone cliff about 2,000 years ago.

name: Vienna, Austria
clues: Two strangers stepped off of a train for one night, / and they talked through my streets until morning's first light. / A big Ferris wheel turned by the old park they found, / in a city where waltzes and coffee abound.
Mozart and Strauss made their music in me, / a capital where the Danube flows free.
Austria's capital, on the Danube I sit, / with a palace called Schönbrunn. That's it.
fact: Before Sunrise was shot in Vienna in 25 days. The couple rides the Riesenrad, the giant Ferris wheel in the Prater park, built in 1897.

name: Martha's Vineyard, USA
clues: A shark with a grin made the beachgoers flee / on a sunny Fourth of July by the sea. / They called me 'Amity,' but that's not my name; / I'm an island where presidents summer, all the same.
Off Cape Cod I sit in the Atlantic blue, / where summer ferries bring tourists through.
An island in Massachusetts, south of Cape Cod's shore, / where Jaws was filmed, and the beaches still roar.
fact: Jaws was filmed on Martha's Vineyard in 1974. The mechanical shark kept breaking in the salt water, so Spielberg showed it far less than planned.

name: Maya Bay, Thailand
clues: A backpacker followed a map to a dream, / a beach hidden by cliffs, with a turquoise gleam. / So many came after, they closed me to rest, / a small island cove, which the movie made best.
I'm near Phuket, where the longtail boats glide, / on a Phi Phi island, with cliffs on each side.
On Phi Phi Leh, in southern Thailand's Andaman Sea, / a short boat ride from Phuket. That's me.
fact: Maya Bay got so many visitors after The Beach that Thailand closed it from 2018 to 2022 to let the coral grow back.

name: Bergen, Norway
clues: A queen with cold hands froze her kingdom one day; / her harbor town's colors were borrowed my way. / My wooden wharf houses are painted so bright, / and it rains here so often, bring boots day and night.
Arendelle's look came from my old harbor front, / in a land of fjords and old Viking stunts.
Norway's second city, on the west coast I stand, / the gateway to the fjords of that land.
fact: Disney's artists visited Norway to design Arendelle. Bergen's colorful Bryggen wharf is one of the clearest inspirations.

name: Skopelos, Greece
clues: A bride mailed three letters to three possible dads, / and they sailed to my island, all dancing like lads. / My chapel sits high on a rock by the sea, / where the wedding was filmed. Now, who could I be?
My pine-covered island's in the Aegean blue, / in the Sporades chain, where the ferries come through.
A Greek island near Skiathos, east of the mainland's coast, / the Mamma Mia! island fans love the most.
fact: The wedding chapel in Mamma Mia! is Agios Ioannis on Skopelos, perched on a rock reached by about 100 steps.

name: Forks, Washington, USA
clues: A girl moved to my town where it rains every day, / and a boy at her school was too pale to play. / He sparkled in sunlight, which hardly comes here, / in my forest of moss where it's cloudy all year.
I'm a small logging town near rainforests and beaches, / out on the Olympic Peninsula's far reaches.
In Washington State, near the Pacific coast, / the Twilight town that fans love the most.
fact: Stephenie Meyer picked Forks by searching online for the rainiest town in the USA. It gets about 3 meters of rain a year.

name: Kenya
clues: A lion cub's uncle pushed his dad off a ledge, / so the cub ran away to the far jungle's edge. / Disney's artists came sketching my grass and my sun, / where the zebras and lions and wildebeest run.
'Hakuna matata' is Swahili, from me, / in East Africa, where safari jeeps roam free.
An East African country right on the equator line, / with Nairobi as capital and the Maasai Mara's shine.
fact: Disney's animators went on a research trip to Kenya before making The Lion King.

name: Hong Kong
clues: A bat-suited hero flew in for a crook; / he leapt off my tower and caught him by hook. / I'm a harbor of skyscrapers glowing at night, / where a tram climbs a peak for the very best sight.
Victoria Harbour, the Star Ferry, dim sum, / on China's south coast, where the busy crowds hum.
A city on China's south coast by the sea, / once British till '97. That's me.
fact: Batman jumps from the IFC tower, one of Hong Kong's tallest buildings.

name: Waterloo, Belgium
clues: A short French emperor lost his last fight / on my muddy green fields, and then lost all his might. / Now my name means you're finished, done in, overthrown, / and a Swedish pop band made it a song of their own.
A lion statue on a hill marks the spot, / just south of Brussels, where the battle was fought.
A Belgian town south of Brussels, where in 1815 / Napoleon met his match. That's the scene.
fact: The Battle of Waterloo was fought on June 18, 1815.

name: Estes Park, Colorado, USA
clues: A writer stayed one night in my big, empty hotel, / in room 217, and he slept none too well. / He went home and wrote of a family snowed in, / with a dad going mad and a twin-sister grin.
My hotel's the Stanley, at the Rockies' front door, / where elk wander my streets and the high mountains soar.
A Colorado mountain town by Rocky Mountain National Park, / northwest of Denver, where the nights get dark.
fact: Stephen King stayed in room 217 of the Stanley Hotel in 1974.

name: Washington, D.C., USA
clues: A treasure hunter said he would steal an old page, / with a map on its back, from a guarded glass cage. / My Capitol's dome and my monument's spire / stand where presidents work and the senators conspire.
The Declaration of Independence is kept here in me, / in the National Archives, by the Potomac, you see.
The capital of the USA, not part of any state, / with the White House and Lincoln. Don't be late.
fact: In National Treasure, the treasure map is written in invisible ink on the back of the Declaration.

from: 🎬 The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants
name: Santorini, Greece
clues: Four friends shared one pair of jeans, mailed around, / and one took them to me, where white houses abound. / My blue domes look down from a crescent of cliff, / where a volcano once blew and left only a rift.
My sunsets in Oia draw crowds every night, / in the Aegean Sea, all blue domes and white.
A Greek island in the Cyclades, shaped like a moon, / a volcano's old rim. Come visit me soon.
fact: Santorini is the rim of a volcano that blew up about 3,600 years ago.

name: Kabul, Afghanistan
clues: Two boys flew their kites through my cold winter sky; / one ran for the string as the kite fluttered by. / Then war came and scattered them far from my hills, / and one came back years later to mend what was ill.
I'm a capital high in the Hindu Kush's shade, / in a landlocked country where old trade routes were made.
The capital of Afghanistan, ringed by mountains, you'll see, / west of Pakistan's border. That's me.
fact: Khaled Hosseini's The Kite Runner came out in 2003 and became a worldwide best seller.

name: Collodi, Italy
clues: A wooden boy's nose grew each time that he lied, / and his author took my name as a pen name with pride. / I'm a small hill village in Tuscany, old, / with a park for the puppet, or so I am told.
Carlo Lorenzini spent childhood summers here, / near Pisa and Lucca, in Tuscany's sphere.
A tiny Tuscan village near Pescia, Italy, / Pinocchio's author's pen name. That's me.
fact: Collodi has a Pinocchio park that opened in 1956.

name: Niagara Falls
clues: I'm shared by two countries, I never stop pouring; / a hero in blue caught a kid near my roaring. / Honeymooners ride boats that get soaked in my spray, / as a river comes crashing down, all night and day.
My Horseshoe Falls thunder on the Canadian side, / between Lake Erie and Ontario, a short, wet ride.
On the US-Canada border, near Buffalo, see? / The most famous waterfalls. That's me.
fact: Niagara Falls is really three waterfalls side by side.

name: Costa Rica
clues: Dinosaurs walk again on an island offshore, / and the scientists' guests came running for the door. / The story says that island lies just off my coast, / where the rainforests, sloths and volcanoes boast.
'Pura vida,' I say, between two oceans wide, / in Central America, with volcanoes inside.
A Central American country, south of Nicaragua, see? / San José is my capital. That's me.
fact: Jurassic Park was actually filmed mostly on Kauai, Hawaii.

name: Bath, England
clues: Jane Austen sent heroines here for a dance, / for gossip and teacups and second-chance romance. / The Romans came first and they soaked in my springs, / and my name is the soak that a bubble tub brings.
My golden stone crescents curve round in a row, / in England's southwest, where the warm waters flow.
A Somerset city near Bristol, with Roman baths too; / Jane Austen once lived here. Now pin me, will you?
fact: Jane Austen lived in Bath from 1801 to 1806.

name: Prince Edward Island, Canada
clues: A red-haired orphan with lots of big words / came to live on a farm with green gables and birds. / My roads and my beaches are red as can be, / on the smallest province, all island and sea.
A bridge eight miles long connects me to land, / in the Gulf of St. Lawrence, with red-colored sand.
Canada's smallest province, an island out east, / near Nova Scotia, where lobster's a feast.
fact: The Green Gables farm in Cavendish is a real place you can visit.

name: Bangkok, Thailand
clues: The wolf pack woke up with a face tattoo, / a monkey on board and no clue what to do. / My river is crowded with longtail boats too, / my temples are golden, my tuk-tuks zoom through.
Pad thai on my corners, gold temples so tall, / where the Chao Phraya River flows through it all.
Thailand's capital city, in Southeast Asia's heat, / with the Grand Palace and spicy food to eat.
fact: Bangkok's full name in Thai is one of the longest place names in the world.

name: Iceland
clues: I played a frozen planet far out in space, / with glaciers and nothing alive in the place. / But I really am fire and ice, it is true: / my volcanoes erupt and my hot springs steam through.
The northern lights dance over my black sand, / in the North Atlantic, a cold island land.
An island nation between Greenland and Norway at sea, / with Reykjavík as capital. That's me.
fact: The ice planet scenes were shot on the Svínafellsjökull glacier.

name: San Diego, USA
clues: Hotshot pilots once trained at my navy base here, / with call signs and shades and a beach volleyball cheer. / My weather is perfect, my zoo is renowned, / and the Mexican border is just a short drive down.
Miramar's where Top Gun first taught pilots to fly, / in sunny Southern California, where the beaches lie.
California's southern city, by the Mexican line, / with a famous zoo, where the weather is fine.
fact: Top Gun: Maverick earned nearly $1.5 billion worldwide in 2022.

from: 🎬 Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
name: Glenfinnan Viaduct, Scotland
clues: A flying blue car chased a red steam train / over my curve of arches, then off again. / I stand in the Highlands where a loch meets the hills, / and steam trains still cross me, giving tourists their thrills.
The Jacobite steam train crosses my 21 arches, / near Fort William, where the Highland mist marches.
A railway viaduct in the Scottish Highlands, see? / At the end of Loch Shiel. That's me.
fact: A real steam train, the Jacobite, still crosses the viaduct in summer.

name: Machu Picchu, Peru
clues: A bear in a blue coat went back to his land / to find his dear aunt, with marmalade in hand. / I'm a lost stone city way up in the clouds, / where llamas graze calmly above all the crowds.
The Incas built me in the Andes up high, / near Cusco, where condors go soaring by.
Peru's famous Inca ruins on a mountain ridge, / reached by the Inca Trail, by train or by bridge.
fact: Michael Bond first had Paddington come from 'darkest Africa', then changed it to Peru.

name: Prague, Czech Republic
clues: A spy's first mission fell apart on my stones, / and he ran through my streets wearing masks, with no phones. / My bridge has old statues, my clock shows the stars, / and a castle looks down on my beer halls and bars.
My astronomical clock puts on a show every hour, / in Central Europe's city of a hundred spires and towers.
The Czech Republic's capital, on the Vltava's bend, / with Charles Bridge across it from end to end.
fact: Prague's Charles Bridge is more than 600 years old.

name: Monaco
clues: A genius in armor raced cars through my streets, / till a villain with electric whips sliced through the seats. / I'm tiny, I'm rich, and my yachts fill the bay, / and my casino's lights glitter all night and all day.
My Grand Prix winds through the tunnels and town, / on the French Riviera, where a prince wears the crown.
The second-smallest country on Earth, by the sea, / on France's south coast near Nice. That's me.
fact: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world, after Vatican City.

from: 📖 Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil
name: Savannah, Georgia, USA
clues: My oak trees drip moss in my leafy green squares, / and a murder in a mansion made headlines and stares. / A book about me sold by millions, they say, / and Forrest Gump sat on a bench of mine one day.
My 22 squares fill the oldest part of town, / on Georgia's coast, where the river runs down.
Georgia's oldest city, near the South Carolina line, / on the Atlantic coast, with Spanish moss so fine.
fact: Forrest Gump's bench sat in Chippewa Square.

name: Mexico City, Mexico
clues: A boy who loved music crossed a bridge made of flowers / to visit his family for just a few hours. / My skulls are all painted, my marigolds glow / on the Day of the Dead, when the candles burn low.
I'm built on a lake where the Aztecs held sway, / now a giant capital, busy night and day.
Mexico's capital, high in the mountains it stands, / once called Tenochtitlan, in Aztec lands.
fact: Pixar's team made several research trips to Mexico for Coco.

name: Warsaw, Poland
clues: A pianist hid in my ruins through the war, / while my buildings were bombed right down to the floor. / An enemy officer heard him and let him be, / and later they rebuilt my Old Town carefully.
Chopin grew up here, by the Vistula's flow, / in Central Europe, where cold winters blow.
The capital of Poland, rebuilt brick by brick, / north of Kraków. Now take your pick.
fact: Warsaw's Old Town was rebuilt after the war and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Inverness, Scotland
clues: A nurse touched a stone and fell back through time, / into kilts and clans and a Highland crime. / Nearby lies a battlefield, sad and still, / and a lake with a monster that folks hunt for still.
Loch Ness is next door, and Culloden's moor too; / I'm the Highlands' capital, with a river running through.
The biggest town in the Scottish Highlands, see? / Where the River Ness meets the sea. That's me.
fact: Diana Gabaldon's first Outlander book came out in 1991.

name: Southern Tunisia
clues: A farm boy looked up at two suns going down, / on a desert planet named after my town. / His home was a crater dug into my ground, / and a hotel today keeps that set safe and sound.
Tatooine borrowed the name of Tataouine, / in North Africa, where the Sahara is seen.
Southern Tunisia, between Algeria and Libya's sand, / where Luke's desert home was filmed on the land.
fact: Luke's home in Matmata is a real hotel you can sleep in.

name: Venice, Italy
clues: My streets are all water, my taxis are boats, / and a gondolier sings as he paddles and floats. / A spy watched a palace sink into my blue, / in a city that's slowly sinking too.
St. Mark's Square floods often, my Grand Canal bends, / in northeast Italy, where the lagoon never ends.
Italy's famous canal city, on the Adriatic Sea, / with gondolas and bridges. That's me.
fact: Venice is built on more than 100 small islands linked by hundreds of bridges.

name: Cinque Terre, Italy
clues: Two sea monsters turned into boys on dry land, / and they dreamed of a Vespa, a trip they had planned. / My villages tumble down cliffs to the sea, / five of them painted as bright as can be.
My name means 'Five Lands,' all linked by a trail, / on Italy's Riviera, where fishing boats sail.
Five colorful villages on the Ligurian coast, / near La Spezia, Italy. That's the place they love most.
fact: Luca's director Enrico Casarosa grew up in Genoa, near the Cinque Terre.

name: Houston, USA
clues: When astronauts get into trouble in space, / they call out my name for a fix, just in case. / I'm a big Texas city of oil and of heat, / where rodeos, rockets and barbecue meet.
Mission Control is here, at NASA's big center, / near the Gulf Coast, a hot place to enter.
The biggest city in Texas, near the Gulf of Mexico's sea, / home of NASA's Mission Control. That's me.
fact: The real line was 'Houston, we've had a problem.'

from: 🎬 Close Encounters of the Third Kind
name: Devils Tower, USA
clues: People had visions of me and couldn't say why; / one sculpted me out of his mashed potato pie. / I'm a tall stump of rock with stripes running down, / where a spaceship touched down and the lights all came round.
The first national monument the USA named, / in Wyoming's northeast, for my columns I'm famed.
A giant rock tower in northeast Wyoming, so tall, / near the Black Hills, the strangest stump of all.
fact: Devils Tower became the first US National Monument, in 1906.

name: Jamaica
clues: We'd never seen snow, but we sent a bobsled / to the Winter Olympics, with no ice to tread. / I'm warm Caribbean, with reggae and sun, / and the world's fastest sprinter was born here to run.
Bob Marley sang here, and jerk chicken's my dish, / in the Caribbean Sea, south of Cuba, as warm as you'd wish.
A Caribbean island nation south of Cuba's shore, / with Kingston as capital and reggae galore.
fact: Jamaica's real bobsled team first raced at the 1988 Winter Olympics in Calgary.

name: Florence, Italy
clues: A professor woke up with no memory, then ran / through my museums and passages, chasing a plan. / My dome is enormous, my David stands tall, / and the Renaissance started inside of my walls.
The Uffizi and the Ponte Vecchio are mine, / in Tuscany, Italy, land of good wine.
Tuscany's capital, on the Arno River, see? / The birthplace of the Renaissance. That's me.
fact: Dante, who wrote the poem Inferno, was born in Florence in 1265.

name: Geneva, Switzerland
clues: A stormy cold summer, a ghost-story game, / and a young writer dreamed up a monster with no name. / By my lake, in a villa, the story was born, / where diplomats gather each day and each morn.
My Jet d'Eau sprays high from a crescent-shaped lake, / in French-speaking Switzerland, where world deals they make.
A Swiss city at the tip of a lake by the French line, / home of the UN in Europe and the Red Cross sign.
fact: Mary Shelley started Frankenstein in 1816 at a villa near Geneva.

name: Angel Falls, Venezuela
clues: An old man tied balloons to his house and took flight / to find a tall waterfall far out of sight. / I'm the tallest on Earth, from a flat-topped rock's height, / and my water turns to mist before it lands outright.
I tumble off a tabletop mountain, in jungle so green, / in South America's north, the highest falls seen.
In Venezuela's Canaima park I fall almost a kilometer free, / the world's tallest waterfall. That's me.
fact: Angel Falls drops 979 meters, the tallest waterfall on Earth.

name: Seattle, USA
clues: A billionaire flew his own helicopter round / over my rainy streets and my coffee-scented ground. / My needle-shaped tower looks over the bay, / and a big coffee chain got its start here one day.
Pike Place has fish flying, the Space Needle's tall, / in the Pacific Northwest, where the raindrops fall.
Washington State's biggest city, on Puget Sound, / with Mount Rainier watching from the ground.
fact: The Fifty Shades books have sold more than 150 million copies.

name: Oxford, England
clues: A girl with an animal soul by her side / ran over my rooftops while zeppelins glide. / My colleges' towers are 'dreaming,' they say, / and students have studied here since a long-ago day.
My 'dreaming spires' and colleges stand / on the Thames, northwest of London, the oldest in the land.
An English city northwest of London, see? / Home of the famous university. That's me.
fact: Oxford is the oldest university in the English-speaking world.

name: Transylvania, Romania
clues: Pack your garlic: there's a count on the hill / who sleeps in a coffin and gives guests a chill. / My mountains are misty, my castles are steep, / and the wolves howl at night while the villagers sleep.
Bran Castle is called the vampire's home, / in the Carpathian Mountains, where the brown bears roam.
A region of central Romania, ringed by peaks, / the land of Dracula that every tourist seeks.
fact: Bran Castle is sold to tourists as 'Dracula's Castle', though Bram Stoker never went to Romania.

name: Skellig Michael, Ireland
clues: A Jedi went hiding on a rock in the sea, / with stone beehive huts that the monks built on me. / Puffins waddle round on my steep stony stair, / and the waves crash so hard that few boats will go there.
Monks lived here a thousand years back, in the spray, / off Ireland's southwest coast, far out in the bay.
A rocky island off County Kerry, Ireland, see? / Luke Skywalker's hideout. That's me.
fact: Monks lived on Skellig Michael more than 1,000 years ago.

name: Havana, Cuba
clues: A racer drove backwards and still won the race, / down my streets full of old cars in candy-colored grace. / My seawall's a long place to sit by the sea, / and cigars and salsa are famous from me.
My 1950s cars cruise the Malecón's wall, / on the Caribbean's biggest island of all.
The capital of Cuba, just south of Florida's coast; / old cars and old buildings are what I have most.
fact: It was the first big Hollywood movie to film in Cuba in decades.

name: Bali, Indonesia
clues: She ate in Italy, prayed far away, / then she found love on my island one day. / My rice fields climb hills in stairs of bright green, / and my temples by the sea make the sunsets serene.
Surfers and yogis love my beaches and Ubud, / in Indonesia, where the incense smells good.
An Indonesian island just east of Java, see? / The Island of the Gods. That's me.
fact: Elizabeth Gilbert's memoir Eat Pray Love has sold more than 10 million copies.

name: Wadi Rum, Jordan
clues: I've played a desert planet with sandworms below, / and I've played planet Mars too, so the movie folks know. / My sand is bright red and my rock towers stand / in a quiet, wide valley of moonlike red land.
Lawrence of Arabia rode through my sand, / in the desert south of a small Middle East land.
A desert valley in southern Jordan, see? / Near Aqaba. Hollywood's Mars is me.
fact: Lawrence of Arabia was also partly filmed in Wadi Rum.

name: Clarksdale, Mississippi, USA
clues: Twin brothers came home with a club to begin, / and the blues played so well that it let vampires in. / A legend says a man sold his soul at my crossroads at night / to play the guitar better than anyone might.
I'm where Highways 61 and 49 cross, / in the Mississippi Delta, where the blues was the boss.
A small town in northwest Mississippi's Delta, see? / A birthplace of the blues. That's me.
fact: Michael B. Jordan plays both twins in Sinners (2025).

name: Reichenbach Falls, Switzerland
clues: A detective and his worst enemy fought / at the edge of my water, and both of them caught / a long fall together, or so readers believed, / till he came back years later and fans were relieved.
I'm a waterfall high in the Swiss Alps' embrace, / near Meiringen, a quiet Bernese place.
In central Switzerland, the falls of a Holmes fight: / Reichenbach Falls, a long mountain flight.
fact: Arthur Conan Doyle sent Sherlock Holmes over the Reichenbach Falls in 1893 to end the stories. Fans protested so much that he brought Holmes back.

name: Zhangjiajie, China
clues: Blue giants rode dragons past mountains that float, / and those mountains were sketched from my pillars of note. / My sandstone towers rise up through the mist, / like a forest of stone that the clouds have kissed.
One of my towers took the film's floating name, / in central China's Hunan, a park of great fame.
Zhangjiajie park, in Hunan, China, see? / The floating mountains were modeled on me.
fact: In 2010 one of Zhangjiajie's sandstone pillars was renamed 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain' after the film.

name: Aswan, Egypt
clues: A detective with a mustache took a cruise on my river, / and a murder on board made the passengers shiver. / Old sailboats with white sails float past my old dam, / and the desert comes right to the water. Here I am.
My dam holds back the world's longest river's flow, / in Egypt's far south, where the hot winds blow.
A city in southern Egypt, on the Nile, see? / Near the High Dam and Lake Nasser. That's me.
fact: Agatha Christie stayed at Aswan's Old Cataract Hotel, and the hotel appears in Death on the Nile.

name: Long Island, New York, USA
clues: A rich man threw parties in his mansion each night / and stared at a green dock light, far out of sight. / My two 'eggs' face each other across a small bay, / where old money and new money went out to play.
My Gold Coast had mansions in the roaring '20s, / just east of New York City, with beaches aplenty.
A long island east of Manhattan, in New York State, / with the Hamptons at its end. Can you place it straight?
fact: F. Scott Fitzgerald based West Egg and East Egg on two peninsulas of Long Island's North Shore, Great Neck and Manhasset Neck.

name: Lhasa, Tibet
clues: A climber escaped from a camp in the war / and walked over mountains to reach my front door. / He tutored a boy who would lead his whole land, / in a palace that sits on a hill, white and grand.
The Potala Palace, red and white, rises here, / on a plateau so high that the sky feels near.
The capital of Tibet, in western China, see? / The Dalai Lamas' old home. That's me.
fact: Heinrich Harrer reached Lhasa in 1946 after escaping a British prison camp in India, and became a tutor and friend to the young Dalai Lama.

name: Kigali, Rwanda
clues: A hotel manager hid more than a thousand inside / when war came to my hills, and so many had died. / Now I'm one of the cleanest cities around, / with plastic bags banned and green hills all round.
The Hôtel des Mille Collines still stands on my hill, / in the land of a thousand hills, quiet and still.
The capital of Rwanda, in East-Central Africa, see? / Not far from the mountain gorillas. That's me.
fact: Paul Rusesabagina sheltered more than 1,200 people at Kigali's Hôtel des Mille Collines in 1994. Rwanda banned plastic bags in 2008.

name: Namib Desert, Namibia
clues: War rigs and madmen raced over my sand, / chasing a truck through a dry, dusty land. / My dunes are some of the tallest and reddest you'll see, / and I meet a cold ocean where the fog rolls in free.
Fury Road was filmed in my wide empty space, / on Africa's southwest coast, a vast, quiet place.
The desert of Namibia, along the Atlantic coast, / with red dunes at Sossusvlei, the ones they photograph most.
fact: Mad Max: Fury Road was filmed in the Namib Desert near Swakopmund. The Namib is often called the oldest desert on Earth.

name: Denali National Park, Alaska, USA
clues: A young man gave away all his money and went / to the wild, to live in an old bus, not a tent. / He didn't come back from my woods and my snow, / near the tallest of peaks North America can show.
My mountain's the tallest in North America, so high, / in the 49th state, where the grizzlies walk by.
A national park in Alaska, with a mountain of the same name: / North America's highest peak is my claim.
fact: Christopher McCandless lived in an abandoned bus near Denali National Park in 1992. The bus was airlifted out in 2020.

name: El Capitan, Yosemite, USA
clues: A climber went up with no rope and no gear, / three thousand feet straight, without showing fear. / My granite's a wall that the sunset turns gold, / in a valley of waterfalls, ancient and old.
Half Dome's my neighbor in a famous national park, / in California's Sierra, where climbers leave their mark.
A giant granite wall in Yosemite Valley, see? / The climbers' biggest prize. That's me.
fact: Alex Honnold climbed El Capitan's Freerider route without ropes in 2017, in just under four hours.

name: Yorkshire Moors, England
clues: Cathy and Heathcliff ran wild on my hills, / through the heather and wind and the cold winter chills. / Three sisters who wrote lived in my parsonage town, / where the moors roll for miles, purple, green and brown.
The Brontë sisters lived in Haworth, near me, / in the north of England, where the wind blows free.
The moors of West Yorkshire, England, rolling and wide, / near Haworth, with Brontë country on every side.
fact: Emily Brontë wrote Wuthering Heights in the parsonage at Haworth, on the edge of the West Yorkshire moors.
